svg.text: nativeshvc: a behaviour-exact console a decompiled game plugs into
Not an emulator: the processors are the game's C, each access its bus time; everything else is nativeshvc, at the hardware's time.

nshvc_main: opens the host, loads the save, powers on, then runs frame after frame; takes the picture and the samples out, brings the
players' devices to the ports, writes the battery save; the game's hooks and overlays. Headless: a script of inputs, shots, dumps, saved states.

each part off until the game asks: Original is the console exactly; the window's picture (sharp bilinear, Mode 7) is native in both
How a game plays through it
The game's main hands its cartridge to nshvc_main: the host opens the window,
sound and controllers, the battery save is loaded and the console powers on.
Dispatch finds the C for the reset vector's address and calls it. Every call, jump
and interrupt vector is reached the same way; an address with no C is fatal.
Each of the original's accesses goes through rd8 / wr8, in its order, costing its
bus time and its cost profile's weight (none with the costs off); its waits are waits.
As the clock passes each H-blank the PPU draws that line and HDMA runs; the
SPC700's and a chip's C are brought up to the same time on their coroutines.
At V-blank the console raises the NMI, which Dispatch hands to the game's
handler C, reads the joypads automatically and ends the frame.
The front end presents the picture on the GPU and resamples the sound, a frame
each 1/60.0988 s (PAL, 1/50.007 s), and brings the players' devices to the ports.
